item.title: Brazilian Church campaigns for housing policies, seeks to expand presence in favelas
item.description: With almost half of Brazilians living in inadequate housing and a rapidly growing number of slums called favelas, the Catholic Church is discussing ways to respond to the new demands of low-income families.

item.title: African Sister leads continental campaign against human trafficking ahead of St. Bakhita’s feast
item.description: As the world prepares to commemorate the Feast of Saint Josephine Bakhita on February 7, an extraordinary movement against human trafficking is gaining momentum across Africa.

item.title: Nicaraguan regime forbids door-to-door pastoral visits in Diocese of León
item.description: In an attack on the Catholic Church, the Nicaraguan regime has forbidden the Diocese of León from promoting pastoral visits to the homes of lay people, informing ecclesial authorities that all activities must be carried out inside Church buildings.

item.title: Pope Leo says the Catholic Church cannot ‘relativize’ its teaching on marriage
item.description: Speaking to members of the Apostolic Tribunal of the Roman Rota, Pope Leo XIV on Monday warned against “a dangerous relativization of truth” when it comes to the Church’s teachings on the indissolubility of the sacrament of marriage.

item.title: Funeral held in Rome for John L. Allen Jr., founding editor-in-chief of Crux
item.description: ROME – A funeral Mass was celebrated for John L. Allen Jr. on Monday in Sant’Eugenio basilica in Rome. The legendary Vatican beat reporter and Church affairs analyst died Thursday, January 22, two days after his 61st birthday, following a lengthy – and by every account heroic – battle with […]

item.title: The first refugee to lead the UN refugee agency meets the pope
item.description: The first refugee to lead the U.N. refugee agency said Monday the world faces “a very difficult moment in history” and is appealing to a common humanity amid dramatic change.

item.title: In surprise move, Spain will grant legal status to thousands of immigrants lacking permission
item.description: Spain’s government announced Tuesday it will grant legal status to potentially hundreds of thousands of immigrants living and working in the country without authorization.

item.title: In divided central Africa, a cardinal presents ‘Family of God’ as path to peace
item.description: Amid the socio-political and economic crises facing the Central Africa region, Congolese Cardinal Fridolin Ambongo Besungu has championed the theological vision of the Church as the "Family of God."

item.title: Spain authorities’ ‘confusion’ prevented priests from administering last rites to train crash victims
item.description: Bishop Jesús Fernández of Córdoba has said that the “confusion” of the authorities prevented priests at the scene of the recent train crash in Adamuz from administering last rites to victims.

item.title: Sarah Mullally confirmed as archbishop of Canterbury, first woman to lead the Church of England
item.description: Sarah Mullally walked into St. Paul’s Cathedral on Wednesday morning as the bishop of London. When she walked out in the afternoon as bells rang out, she was the spiritual leader of millions of Anglicans around the world.
